title: Verbal noun + pronoun: Gad fhaicinn
question: What does 'tha mi gad fhaicinn' mean?
explanation: 'Gad' is 'ga' + 'do' (your): the object pronoun goes before the verbal noun. 'Gam' would mean me and 'ga' would mean him.

title: Gerundive construction: A' feuchainn ris
question: What does 'a' feuchainn ris' mean?
explanation: 'Feuchainn ri' means trying or attempting; 'ris' is 'ri' + 'e' (it).

title: Causative: Leig mi leis falbh
question: What does 'leig mi leis falbh' mean?
explanation: 'Leig le' means let or allow. 'Leis' is 'le' + 'e' (him); 'leam' would mean me.

title: Double object construction: Thug mi leabhar dha
question: What does 'thug mi leabhar dha' mean?
explanation: 'Dha' is 'do' + 'e' (to him). To her is 'dhi', to me is 'dhomh' and to them is 'dhaibh'.

title: Impersonal construction: Bhiodh fios agam
question: What does 'bhiodh fios agam' mean?
explanation: 'Bhiodh' is the conditional of 'bi', so 'bhiodh fios agam' means 'I would know'. 'Tha fios agam' is I know and 'bha' is I knew.

title: Copular: Is tidsear i
question: What does 'is tidsear i' mean?
explanation: 'Is' + noun + pronoun says what someone is. 'I' is she and 'e' would be he; the past would be 'bu tidsear i'.

title: Existential perfect: Air a bhith ann
question: What does 'tha e air a bhith ann' mean?
explanation: 'Tha ... air a bhith ann' is the perfect: has been there. 'Bha' would make it 'had been' and 'bha e ann' is simply 'was there'.

title: Conditional: Nan robh e toilichte
question: Which is the way to say 'If he were happy' (but he is not)?
explanation: 'Nan robh' introduces an unreal condition. 'Ma tha' is a real 'if he is', 'ma bhitheas' is 'if he will be' and 'nuair a bha' is 'when he was'.

title: Conditional perfect: Bhiodh mi air dhol
question: What does 'bhiodh mi air dhol' mean?
explanation: 'Bhiodh' + 'air' + verbal noun is the conditional perfect. 'Bidh' would make it future and 'bha' would make it past.

title: Negative conditional: Nach canadh tu
question: What does 'nach canadh tu sin?' mean?
explanation: 'Nach' begins a negative question and 'canadh' is the conditional of 'ràdh', so it means 'wouldn't you say that?'. 'An canadh tu sin?' is the positive question.

title: Reported speech: Gur e Iain
question: What does 'thuirt e gur e Iain a bha ann' mean?
wrong1: He asked if it was Iain
wrong3: He said it will be Iain
explanation: 'Gur e' introduces a reported statement with the copula, and 'a bha ann' puts it in the past: 'it was Iain'. 'A th' ann' would be present.

title: Reported speech: Gun tigeadh
question: What does 'thuirt i gun tigeadh i' mean?
wrong3: She asked if she would come
explanation: 'Gun' introduces a reported statement and 'tigeadh' is the conditional of 'thig', which after a past verb of saying means 'would come'.

title: Question in reported speech: An robh?
question: What does 'dh'fhaighnich mi an robh thu ann' mean?
correct: I asked if you were there
wrong1: I asked if you are there
wrong2: I asked if you will be there
wrong3: I asked if you would be there
explanation: 'An robh' is the past form of 'an' (whether) in reported yes/no questions. 'A bheil' would be present and 'am bi' would be future.

title: Negative reported speech: Nach robh
question: What does 'thuirt i nach robh i sgìth' mean?
wrong2: She said she wouldn't be tired
wrong3: She asked whether she was tired
explanation: 'Nach' introduces a negative reported statement and 'robh' makes it past. 'Nach eil' would be present and 'nach bhiodh' would be conditional.

title: Relative clauses: A bh'ann
question: What does 'an t-àm a bh'ann' mean?
explanation: 'A bh'ann' is the past relative form: 'an t-àm a bh'ann' = 'the time that was'.

title: Relative future: A bhios
question: What does 'an latha a bhios sinn ann' mean?
correct: The day that we will be there
wrong1: The day that we were there
wrong2: The day that we are there
wrong3: The day that we would be there
explanation: 'A bhios' is the future relative form of 'bi'. 'A bha' is past, 'a tha' is present and 'a bhiodh' is conditional.

title: Verbal noun: Ri dhèanamh
question: What does 'tha rudeigin agam ri dhèanamh' mean?
explanation: 'Ri' + verbal noun after a noun says what is still to be done: 'rudeigin ri dhèanamh' is something to do.

title: Temporal clause: Nuair a bha
question: What does 'nuair a bha i òg' mean?
explanation: 'Nuair a' introduces temporal clauses and 'bha' marks the past: 'when she was young'.

title: Temporal: Mu dheireadh
question: What does 'mu dheireadh' mean?
explanation: 'Mu dheireadh' (around the end) means 'finally' or 'at last'.

title: Temporal: Roimhe sin
question: What does 'roimhe sin' mean?
explanation: 'Roimhe sin' means 'before that'. 'Às dèidh sin' is after that.

title: Temporal: Gus am bi
question: What does 'gus am bi e deiseil' mean?
explanation: 'Gus an' (here 'gus am' before 'b') means 'until', and 'bi' gives the future sense: 'until he is ready'.

title: Negative question: Nach tuirt mi
question: What does 'nach tuirt mi sin riut?' mean?
explanation: 'Nach' begins a negative question and 'tuirt' is the past of 'ràdh', so it asks 'didn't I say?'.

title: Cleft construction: Is mise
question: What does 'is mise a tha sgìth' mean?
correct: It is I who am tired
wrong1: It is you who are tired
wrong2: It is he who is tired
wrong3: It was I who was tired
explanation: Cleft constructions use the copula for emphasis: 'is' + emphatic pronoun + 'a tha'. 'Is tusa' would be you and 'bu mhise ... a bha' would be past.

title: Cleft with antecedent: Is e Iain
question: What does 'is e Iain a thubhairt sin' mean?
correct: It was Iain who said that
wrong1: It was Iain who was told that
wrong2: It is Iain who will say that
explanation: The cleft puts Iain in focus and the relative verb 'a thubhairt' (said) carries the past tense.

title: Cleft: Is ann Diluain
question: What does 'is ann Diluain a thig e' mean?
correct: It is on Monday that he will come
wrong1: It is on Monday that he came
wrong2: It is on Tuesday that he will come
wrong3: It is on Monday that he would come
explanation: 'Is ann' puts the time expression first for emphasis, and the relative 'a thig' is future. 'Dimàirt' is Tuesday.

title: Infinitive: Tha e doirbh a ràdh
question: What does 'tha e doirbh a ràdh' mean?
wrong2: It will be difficult to say
wrong3: It would be difficult to say
explanation: 'Tha e' + adjective + 'a' + verbal noun means 'it is ... to ...'; 'bha' would make it past.

title: Adjective + dhen: Tha mi sgìth dhen obair
question: What does 'tha mi sgìth dhen obair' mean?
correct: I am tired of the work
wrong1: I was tired of the work
wrong2: I will be tired of the work
wrong3: I would be tired of the work
explanation: 'Sgìth dhen' means tired of; 'tha' marks the present.

title: Iterative: A-rithist 's a-rithist
question: What does 'a-rithist 's a-rithist' mean?
explanation: 'A-rithist 's a-rithist' means 'repeatedly' or 'again and again'.

title: Habitual past: Bhiodh mi a' snàmh
question: What does 'bhiodh mi a' snàmh an-uairsin' mean?
explanation: Habitual past uses 'bhiodh' (would) + progressive. 'Bha mi a' snàmh' is a single ongoing event.

title: Frequentative: Bidh gu tric
question: What does 'bidh mi gu tric ann' mean?
explanation: 'Gu tric' (often) with 'bidh' expresses a frequent habit; 'bha' would make it past.

title: Durative: Fad greis
question: What does 'bha sin a' dol air adhart fad greis' mean?
correct: That was going on for a while
wrong1: That is going on for a while
wrong2: That will go on for a while
wrong3: That was going on all day
explanation: 'Fad greis' (for a while) marks duration, and 'bha' makes it past.

title: Future: Thig i a-rithist
question: What does 'chan eil i ann a-nis, ach thig i a-rithist' mean?
correct: She isn't here now, but she will come again
wrong1: She wasn't here, but she came again
wrong2: She isn't here now, but she came again
wrong3: She wasn't here, and she will not come again
explanation: 'Chan eil' is present negative and 'thig' is the future of 'thig'.

title: Aspect: Thòisich air
question: What does 'thòisich e air an obair' mean?
explanation: 'Thòisich air' means began; 'chrìochnaich' would be finished.

title: Aspect: Chrìochnaich
question: What does 'chrìochnaich e an leabhar' mean?
explanation: 'Chrìochnaich' is the past of 'crìochnaich' (finish); 'thòisich' would be started.
